propositions: The completion-verify agent step has no loop breaker: tool_step_limit is never set on the primary RunRequest in build_agent_request, so repetitive tool cycles consume the full step budget and die with no verdict instead of landing one

A windowed distinct-ratio discriminator (window 24, trip condition ≤0.50) fires on all three pathological runs (calls 88/151/196) and never on healthy breadth (minimum ratio 0.833), separating genuine cycles from legitimate evidence-gathering

The existing max_consecutive_repeat metric is inverted on real data: a 4-call cycle scores 1 while healthy breadth scores 5, making it unsuitable as an actuator trigger without fixing the underlying metric first

When a runaway is detected, the run must be aborted and routed into the shipped bounded recovery + tool-free finalizer (completion_recovery.py:453-521) to emit a completion_verdict from fresh per-criterion evidence rather than landing on the poisoned loop history

The detected runaway error must be classified by interpret_failure with its own typed branch ahead of the generic LLMUnavailableError fallback, so runaway loops are not misreported as provider outages

Both kill paths (request_limit and tool_calls_limit) must be bounded as failure conditions: the discriminator acts on tool_calls, so a runaway burning calls without burning requests is caught by the same signal
